importance_ranking.reason: Visual sub-type variation is extreme — conical, hypar, barrel vault, flat canopy, and umbrella structures are visually non-interchangeable. Buyers identify the required structure type from the image before reading any text; wrong shape or type is an immediate skip.

Fabric material (PVC vs PVDF vs PTFE) and structure type (car parking vs pool cover vs walkway) are primary shortlisting criteria — they determine suitability, lifespan, and price tier. Buyers discover across spec tiers during search, not just confirm a known spec.

Per-sq-ft rate comparison is the dominant commercial behaviour among Indian construction buyers once structure type and fabric material match. Price changes substantially with fabric grade (PVC vs PVDF vs PTFE) and structure complexity, making it a primary shortlisting signal after spec confirmation.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per piece for standard configurations or per project for large-span installations — per sq ft vs per piece creates real price comparison confusion and must be shown alongside price.
importance_ranking.reason: Price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit. Per sq ft is dominant but per piece and per project variants exist in the market, creating genuine buyer confusion if unit is not displayed.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: The Indian modular tensile structure market is highly fragmented across regional fabricators with no dominant brand that buyers search for by name — buyers search by structure type and fabric spec, not manufacturer name.
importance_ranking.reason: Installation track record, fabrication capability, and warranty are evaluated during vendor selection for a semi-permanent structure, but company identity is not a primary shortlisting gate — it is assessed after visual, spec, and price shortlisting.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the product class — PVC, PVDF, PTFE, and HDPE are non-interchangeable materials with dramatically different price points, lifespans, and application suitability, making this the primary price-driving configurator.

Defines the application configuration (car parking vs pool cover vs walkway vs food court) — non-interchangeable across buyer requirements and drives significant price variation due to differing geometry, load requirements, and anchoring complexity.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Span width and total coverage area are primary cost drivers — larger spans require heavier structural frames and more complex engineering, directly affecting per-sq-ft pricing and seller capacity to supply.
Buyers frequently specify colour as a visual and branding requirement (white, blue, green, beige are standard options), and sellers need this to confirm stock availability or fabrication lead time.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Defines the geometric form of the structure — conical, dome, flat canopy, and pergola require different fabrication processes and materials, enabling sellers to immediately determine supply capability and price range.

Defines the installation context (car parking, EV charging, restaurant terrace, stadium) which determines structural load requirements, span needs, and compliance considerations that sellers must assess before responding.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Fabric material (PVC vs PVDF vs PTFE) is the single most important spec for sellers to determine price, fabrication process, and lifespan commitment — a buyer requesting PTFE for a permanent installation is a fundamentally different supply requirement from a PVC temporary shade.
